research_concepts: largest gainer in absent player's primary play types
teammate minutes / initiations / same-position minutes as predictors
methodological_questions: Does the most similar-profile teammate more often than chance become the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types?
Do simple heuristics (most minutes, most initiations, most same-position minutes) predict the largest gainer as well as or better than similarity?
What is the chance-level hit rate given roster size and ties, and how do we avoid regression to the mean in picking the 'largest gainer' among many teammates?
What is the unit of analysis (148 spells vs 11 cases) and how are dependent spells clustered by player and team?

historical_evidence.finding: Exploratory, non-confirmatory map of about 23 absences. Mean replacement similarity was ABSORBED +0.863 vs CASCADE +0.848, and Spearman(sim, -gap) = -0.19 (wrong-signed). Embiid 2023-24 cascaded despite a Reed similarity of 0.94. Recorded verdict: null (B_powered_null). Recorded evidence: 'Similarity does not separate absorption from cascade; almost always findable.' Sample and power NOT_RECORDED; adjudication was automated, not human. No validation recorded.

Real absences move the association structure (V1 confirmed: 16/23 above own-null p95). The leave-one-out simulation did not predict the magnitude of the change: V2a Spearman +0.288 p=0.077 CI [-0.244,+0.667] FAIL; V2b +0.253 p=0.115 FAIL. This was recorded under limitation small_sample.
Absence of a shaper displaces the team fingerprint (D_A) more than a usage-matched role occupant (n=96 pairs, +0.115, t=6.35). This concerns team-level displacement, not which teammate gains.
Connector absence displaces team offensive identity more than usage-matched non-organizer absence (n=96 pairs). Recorded risks: MECHANICAL_FLOOR and SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using replacement-profile similarity to separate absorption from cascade after a player sits
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as an adequately powered null (B_powered_null): similarity is almost always findable, so it does not discriminate. The sign was wrong, and the label has a LABEL_ERROR risk.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Predicting the magnitude of absence-driven reorganization with leave-one-out simulation (V2a/V2b)
failed_approaches.why: Confidence intervals spanned zero with only about 23 cases (limitation small_sample); the record's status is untestable.

evidence_establishes: FAM:SF-CHT-052 reports, in an exploratory map of about 23 absences, that profile similarity did not separate absorbing from cascading outcomes (the similarity gap was +0.015 and the correlation was wrong-signed).
Team-level fingerprint displacement under absence of shapers or connectors is recorded as supported (FAM:SF-PAP-014, FAM:SF-APPS-088), so absences do reorganize offence in aggregate.
Predicting the magnitude of reorganization from simulation was not achieved at about 23 cases (FAM:SF20).
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests whether the closest-profile teammate is the single largest gainer in the absent player's primary types. FAM:SF-CHT-052 tests a related but different outcome (absorb vs cascade).
No retrieved record compares similarity with the minutes, initiations or same-position-minutes heuristics.
No hit rate against a chance baseline was recorded, and nothing on n=148 spells or the 11 cases in the current task.
FAM:SF-CHT-052's sample and power are NOT_RECORDED, its adjudication was automated, and it was labeled non-confirmatory. So the 'powered null' label is itself uncertain.
own_inferences: The prior is that the closest-profile teammate is often not the largest gainer. Similarity is almost always high (about 0.85 for both outcomes), so it has little discriminating power. A top-1 hit rate is likely to be near 1/(k teammates), perhaps modestly above it.

The minutes, initiations and same-position-minutes heuristics are correlated with each other and with similarity, because high-minute teammates are the most similar to a primary initiator. They will therefore be hard to separate without a joint model.
The question bundles four predictors into one hypothesis, so a 'supported' result for any one is likely to be a multiplicity artifact.

'Largest gainer' is a max over teammates, which is prone to regression to the mean and to mechanical effects. Teammates with high minutes or initiations have more room to gain in absolute counts, and a small absent-player base means sparse primary-type possessions.

11 cases is the effective unit for confirmatory inference if cases are independent absence events. The 148 spells are probably clustered within a smaller number of players and teams, which makes the independence of 148 doubtful.
uncertainties: It is unclear how the 148 spells relate to the 11 cases (for example, whether the 11 are cases passing a primary-type exposure gate).
The definition of 'primary types' of the absent player is not given (top 2? share threshold?).
The similarity metric used in FAM:SF-CHT-052 and its ties to the current definition are unknown.
Whether the 2025-26 data, if used, were seen in the earlier exploratory work is not known.
The retrieved records give no minimum-exposure rules for gain estimation.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history, the plan would be a straightforward confirmatory test. FAM:SF-CHT-052 (recorded verdict null, wrong-signed, exploratory) and FAM:SF20 (small-sample failure of magnitude prediction) lowered the predicted support probability and moved the decision from 'proceed' to 'proceed_with_changes'. The design is a pre-registered, chance-referenced comparison of predictors with the 11 cases treated as the confirmatory limit, and the 148 spells used for secondary clustered analysis.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 11 cases (and 148 clustered spells) give very low power to detect a top-1 hit rate modestly above chance; an 11-case hit count has a wide interval.
Primary-type possessions without the absent player are sparse for many spells, so gain estimates for the largest gainer are noisy.
Four predictors are bundled (similarity, minutes, initiations, same-position minutes); any 'a predictor wins' claim needs correction or one pre-specified primary predictor.

prior_work.summary: FAM:SF-CHT-052 is an exploratory null on a related outcome (similarity vs absorb/cascade, about 23 absences). No retrieved work tests largest-gainer identity or the minutes/initiation heuristics. Related absence work (FAM:SF-PAP-014, FAM:SF-APPS-088) supports team-level displacement only.

risks.text: 11 cases (148 spells that are probably clustered by player and team) are insufficient for a modest effect over a roughly 1/k chance rate.
The largest gainer is a maximum over noisy teammate gains, so extreme gains partly reflect noise; high-minute and high-initiation teammates are over-represented among candidates.
Few primary-type possessions per spell and per teammate make gain estimates unstable.
Teammate predictors are collinear; role, lineup substitutions, opponent, injury/trade timing and replacement call-ups confound who gains.
The chance rate of picking the largest gainer depends on the number of rotation teammates (about 7-9); hit rates must be compared with that baseline and with a random/minutes-only baseline.
Four predictor definitions and a flexible 'primary types' definition create many forking paths.
Similarity is almost always findable (FAM:SF-CHT-052), so a profile-similarity measure may have little discriminating range; initiation-type labels derive from play-by-play rules.
Play-type classification and the 'absorb vs cascade' labels recorded in FAM:SF-CHT-052 are partly automated and could misclassify teammate gains.
If the pre-absence profile or 'primary types' are computed using data that include the absence spell, the predictor and outcome are not independent.
Four seasons with roster and rule changes mean pre-absence profiles may drift; the 2025-26 data were partial before the stated completion dates.

design.estimand: For each qualifying absence case, whether the teammate with the highest pre-absence profile similarity (primary predictor: cosine similarity of play-type initiation shares, computed on pre-absence games only) is the teammate with the largest gain in the absent player's primary play-type possessions per 100 team possessions (absent vs present baseline). Primary statistic is the top-1 hit rate against the exact chance rate from the number of eligible teammates in each case; secondary statistics are the top-2 hit rate and the rank of the similarity-predicted teammate among gainers. Heuristics (most minutes, most initiations, most same-position minutes) are reported as comparators and are not primary hypotheses.
design.unit: Absence case (player-season spell group meeting exposure gates) is the confirmatory unit, n=11; the 148 spells are a secondary unit analysed with player/team clustering (cluster bootstrap or mixed model).
design.sample: NBA 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs as the primary set. The 2025-26 regular season and playoffs are held out as a confirmatory set only if the cases are not already part of the earlier exploratory work (FAM:SF-CHT-052 involved about 23 absences). Eligibility, fixed before looking at outcomes: the absent player has at least a minimum number of primary-type possessions before the absence; at least k rotation teammates; a minimum number of games absent; the teammate pool is defined from pre-absence rotation data.
design.power: With 11 cases and a chance rate of about 1/8, the exact binomial test has power of only about 0.5-0.7 for a true hit rate of 0.40 and very low power for 0.25. State that only large effects are detectable; report exact (Clopper-Pearson) intervals; if the 148 spells give materially more independent cases after clustering, use them for the main analysis and the 11 cases as a sensitivity set. Interpret a non-significant result as inconclusive unless the interval excludes a hit rate of 0.35.
design.controls: Chance baseline from the actual teammate count per case (permutation: randomly pick a teammate within the case). Compare similarity with the minutes-only and initiations-only predictors in a conditional logit with case-level fixed effects. Control for position overlap and teammate baseline primary-type share. Gains measured as per-100-possession rates with shrinkage (empirical Bayes) to limit regression to the mean. Pre-absence profile and primary types estimated only from games before the spell, with a split-half reliability check on the profile.
design.falsification: Placebo: replace the absent player with a matched player who is present (a pseudo-absence with matched minutes and role) and test whether the similarity-predicted teammate is the largest gainer at the same hit rate. Also permute teammate labels within case. A real effect needs a hit rate above both the permutation chance level and the placebo. In line with FAM:SF-CHT-052, an observed hit rate not above the minutes-only baseline will be reported as a null.
design.multiplicity: One primary hypothesis (similarity top-1 hit vs chance). The three heuristics are secondary and are reported with Holm correction across the four predictors. Exact definitions of primary types (top 2 types by share) and similarity metric are fixed before analysis; any alternative definition is labeled exploratory.
design.decision_rule: Supported: exact one-sided binomial p<0.05 against the case-specific chance rate, the hit rate is at least 0.35, similarity beats the placebo and the minutes-only predictor in the same direction, and the clustered analysis on the 148 spells agrees. Rejected: the 95% interval excludes a hit rate of 0.35 (or the 148-spell clustered interval excludes a meaningful lift over chance). Otherwise inconclusive. A hit rate that matches the minutes-only predictor is reported as 'no added information from similarity'.
design.data_version: NBA per-game files (play-by-play, rotations, starters, matchup minutes, box scores) and the play-type possession graph as available on 2026-11-01; 2022-23 to 2024-25 full; 2025-26 regular season complete as of 2026-04-13 and playoffs as of 2026-06-21. Freeze a file hash and the graph snapshot before analysis.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

messages.content:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}

The details on FAM:SF-CHT-052 are unclear, especially the sample and power fields, so I'm leaning toward one read to be sure, even though the reply has to be a single JSON object.
